independence_basis: separate process, fresh session, clean checkout, integrity verified

findings.evidence: run_cmd and _run call communicate(timeout), then on TimeoutExpired call killpg and communicate() with no timeout. killpg does not reach a child that called setsid(), and the sweep_orphans() that would kill it comes only after communicate returns. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R10/hang.py: run_cmd([python,-c,'Popen(["setsid","sleep","30"])'], '.', 3) had not returned after 15 s. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R10/worker.py: run_worker(command 'setsid sleep 40 & echo done', timeout_s=3) had not returned after 20 s. Any gate, test or worker child can keep the driver blocked indefinitely (a malicious implementer can also open its CLI's stdout through /proc/$PPID/fd/1). The only recovery is killing the driver, which moves the orphan outside the subreaper tree (see R10-02).
findings.suggested_fix: After TimeoutExpired (and before any blocking second communicate), killpg then sweep_orphans() first, and bound the second communicate with a timeout (or close the pipes and kill). Do the same in _run. Add tests where a setsid child keeps stdout open.
findings.title: Timeout path calls communicate() without a timeout before the R8-01 orphan sweep: a setsid descendant holding stdout hangs the driver indefinitely and the sweep is never reached

findings.evidence: Probe: a driver running run_worker(sleep 300) was killed with SIGKILL. The worker kept running (ppid 1, its own session), and a new driver's sweep_orphans() returned {'contained': True, 'killed': 0}. Workers run with start_new_session, so a launcher timeout that kills the driver (or R10-01 forcing one) leaves them alive while the resumed run records contained=true.
findings.suggested_fix: Record each worker's/command's session id (pid) in state before launch. At run start, scan /proc for live processes in those sessions and kill them, or refuse contained=true until none is left.
findings.title: contained=true is recorded although workers or orphans of an earlier, killed driver process are still running (outside the subreaper tree); documented limitation, but realistic and reachable through R10-01
